# 📝 Code Quality Standards

## Naming Conventions

### Class Naming

```java
// ✅ Service classes
@Service
public class InstanceService { }
@Service
public class PaymentService { }

// ✅ Repository classes (interface)
@Repository
public interface InstanceRepository extends JpaRepository<Instance, UUID> { }

// ✅ Controller classes
@RestController
public class InstanceController { }
@RestController
public class PaymentController { }

// ✅ DTO classes (request/response)
public class CreateInstanceRequest { }
public class InstanceResponse { }
public class InstanceCreatedResponse { }
public class InstanceListResponse { }

// ✅ Enum classes
public enum InstanceStatus {
    CREATING, RUNNING, SUSPENDED, DELETED
}

public enum DatabaseEngine {
    MYSQL, POSTGRESQL, MONGODB, REDIS, CASSANDRA, SQLSERVER
}

// ✅ Exception classes
public class InstanceCreationException extends ApiException { }
public class DockerOperationException extends ApiException { }

// ✅ Event classes
public class InstanceCreatedEvent extends ApplicationEvent { }
public class InstanceDeletedEvent extends ApplicationEvent { }

// ✅ Listener classes (EventListener)
@Component
public class InstanceEventListener { }

// ✅ Utility classes
public class InstanceUtil { }
public class PasswordUtil { }

// ✅ Configuration classes
@Configuration
public class DockerConfig { }
@Configuration
public class SecurityConfig { }

// ✅ Mapper classes (if using MapStruct)
@Mapper
public interface InstanceMapper {
    InstanceResponse toResponse(Instance instance);
}
```

### Method Naming

```java
// ✅ Getter/Setter (auto-generated by Lombok)
private String name;
// generates getName(), setName(String)

// ✅ Query methods (repository)
Optional<User> findByEmail(String email);
List<Instance> findByUserId(UUID userId);
List<Instance> findByStatusAndEngine(InstanceStatus status, String engine);

// ✅ Business logic methods
public Instance createInstance(CreateInstanceRequest req, User user)
public void suspendInstance(UUID id)
public List<Instance> getUserInstances(UUID userId)
public boolean canUserCreateInstance(UUID userId, int count)

// ✅ Test methods
void createInstance_whenValidRequest_succeeds()
void listInstances_withPagination_returnsPagedResults()
void deleteInstance_withInvalidId_throws404()
```

### Variable Naming

```java
// ✅ Use meaningful names
boolean canCreateInstance = paymentApi.canUserCreateInstance(userId, count);
String databaseConnectionUrl = buildConnectionString(host, port, dbName);
List<Instance> activeInstances = instanceRepository.findActiveByUserId(userId);

// ❌ Avoid abbreviated/unclear names
boolean b = paymentApi.canUserCreateInstance(uid, cnt);
String connStr = buildConnectionString(h, p, db);
List<Instance> active = repo.findActive(id);

// ✅ Use descriptive loop variables
for (Instance instance : instances) {
    // clear meaning
}

// ❌ Avoid single letters (except index)
for (Instance i : instances) {
    // unclear
}

// ✅ Constants in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
private static final int DEFAULT_INSTANCE_MEMORY_MB = 256;
private static final String DEFAULT_DOCKER_NETWORK = "crudcloud-network";
private static final long JWT_EXPIRATION_MS = 86400000;
```

## Documentation & Comments

### Javadoc Requirements

```java
// ✅ Public methods MUST have Javadoc
/**
 * Creates a new database instance with specified configuration.
 * 
 * Validates plan limits before creation and publishes InstanceCreatedEvent
 * on successful creation. The generated database password is returned in
 * the response and is only shown this one time.
 * 
 * @param request the instance creation request containing engine type, name, memory
 * @param user the authenticated user creating the instance
 * @return the created Instance with status CREATING
 * @throws PlanLimitExceededException if user has reached plan limit
 * @throws DockerOperationException if Docker container creation fails
 * @throws ValidationException if request validation fails
 */
public Instance createInstance(CreateInstanceRequest request, User user) {
    // Implementation...
}

// ✅ Complex logic should have inline comments
public void processInstanceStatus() {
    // Validate plan limits BEFORE expensive Docker operations
    if (!paymentApi.canUserCreateInstance(user.getId(), currentCount)) {
        throw new PlanLimitExceededException("Limit reached");
    }
    
    // Start Docker container first to fail fast if infrastructure unavailable
    String containerId = dockerService.startContainer(config);
    
    // Update status to RUNNING only after successful Docker startup
    instance.setStatus(InstanceStatus.RUNNING);
    instanceRepository.save(instance);
}

// ✅ Event listeners should document what they do
/**
 * Listens for InstanceCreatedEvent and sends notification email to user.
 * 
 * This runs asynchronously after instance creation event is published.
 * If email sending fails, it logs warning but does not block instance creation.
 */
@EventListener
public void onInstanceCreated(InstanceCreatedEvent event) {
    // Implementation...
}

// ❌ Avoid obvious comments
String engine = request.getEngine();  // Get engine - unnecessary!

// ✅ Comment the WHY, not the WHAT
// Fetch with LAZY loading to avoid N+1 queries when iterating instances
@OneToMany(fetch = FetchType.LAZY, mappedBy = "user")
private List<Instance> instances;
```

### Module-Level Documentation

```java
/**
 * Instance Management Module
 * 
 * Responsible for:
 * - Creating and managing database instances via Docker
 * - Tracking instance state and statistics
 * - Orchestrating container lifecycle operations
 * 
 * Communication:
 * - Publishes: InstanceCreatedEvent, InstanceDeletedEvent
 * - Consumes: PaymentModuleApi for plan validation
 * 
 * Package structure:
 * - controller: REST endpoints for instance management
 * - service: Business logic (InstanceService, DockerOrchestrationService)
 * - repository: Data access (InstanceRepository)
 * - model: Domain entities (Instance, InstanceStatus)
 * - dto: Request/response objects
 * - exception: Instance-specific exceptions
 * - api: Public module API (InstanceModuleApi)
 */
package com.riwi.crudcloud.instance;
```

## Code Style

### Using Lombok

```java
// ✅ Use Lombok for boilerplate reduction
@Data
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
@Builder
public class User {
    private UUID id;
    private String email;
    private String password;
    private LocalDateTime createdAt;
    
    // Lombok generates: getters, setters, equals, hashCode, toString, builder
}

// ✅ Be specific with Lombok annotations
@Data
@Builder
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
public class Instance {
    private UUID id;
    private String name;
    private String engine;
    
    // ❌ Avoid including toString for sensitive fields
    @ToString.Exclude
    private String connectionPassword;  // Never show in logs
}
```

### Method Organization

```java
// ✅ Keep methods focused (single responsibility)
public Instance createInstance(CreateInstanceRequest request, User user) {
    validateRequest(request);
    validatePlanLimits(user);
    Instance instance = buildInstance(request, user);
    return saveAndOrchestrate(instance);
}

private void validateRequest(CreateInstanceRequest request) {
    // Validation logic
}

private void validatePlanLimits(User user) {
    // Plan validation logic
}

private Instance buildInstance(CreateInstanceRequest request, User user) {
    // Instance building logic
}

private Instance saveAndOrchestrate(Instance instance) {
    // Save and orchestration logic
}

// ❌ Avoid large methods doing multiple things
public Instance createInstance(CreateInstanceRequest request, User user) {
    // 100+ lines of mixed validation, building, saving, orchestration
}
```

### Exception Handling

```java
// ✅ Catch specific exceptions
try {
    String containerId = dockerService.startContainer(config);
} catch (DockerOperationException e) {
    logger.error("Failed to start Docker container", e);
    throw new InstanceCreationException("Container startup failed", e);
}

// ❌ Avoid catching generic Exception
try {
    // code
} catch (Exception e) {  // Too broad!
    throw new RuntimeException(e);
}

// ✅ Chain exceptions to preserve stack trace
try {
    userRepository.save(user);
} catch (DataIntegrityViolationException e) {
    logger.warn("User already exists: {}", user.getEmail());
    throw new UserAlreadyExistsException(user.getEmail(), e);
}
```

### Null Safety

```java
// ✅ Use Optional instead of null checks
public User findByEmail(String email) {
    return userRepository.findByEmail(email);
    // Returns Optional<User>
}

// ✅ Chain Optional operations
public UserResponse getProfile(String email) {
    return userRepository.findByEmail(email)
        .map(this::toResponse)
        .orElseThrow(() -> new UserNotFoundException(email));
}

// ✅ Use annotations for clarity
@Nullable
public String getOptionalField(Instance instance) {
    return instance.getOptionalField();
}

@NotNull
public String getRequiredField(Instance instance) {
    return instance.getName();
}

// ❌ Avoid excessive null checks
if (user != null) {
    if (user.getInstances() != null) {
        if (user.getInstances().size() > 0) {
            // Logic here
        }
    }
}

// ✅ Use Optional instead
user.getInstances()
    .ifPresent(instances -> processInstances(instances));
```

### Logging

```java
// ✅ Use SLF4J with Lombok @Slf4j
@Service
@Slf4j
public class InstanceService {
    
    public Instance createInstance(CreateInstanceRequest request) {
        logger.info("Creating instance: {}", request.getName());
        
        try {
            Instance instance = buildInstance(request);
            logger.debug("Instance built with configuration: {}", instance.getId());
            
            return instanceRepository.save(instance);
        } catch (DockerOperationException e) {
            logger.error("Docker operation failed for instance: {}", request.getName(), e);
            throw new InstanceCreationException("Creation failed", e);
        }
    }
}

// ❌ Avoid System.out.println
System.out.println("Instance created");  // BAD!

// ❌ Avoid printStackTrace
catch (Exception e) {
    e.printStackTrace();  // BAD! Use logger instead
}
```

## Best Practices

### ✅ DO: Follow DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)

```java
// ❌ REPEATED CODE
public Instance createInstance(CreateInstanceRequest req, User user) {
    if (req.getName() == null || req.getName().isBlank()) {
        throw new ValidationException("Name required");
    }
    // ... create instance
}

public void updateInstance(UUID id, UpdateInstanceRequest req) {
    if (req.getName() == null || req.getName().isBlank()) {
        throw new ValidationException("Name required");
    }
    // ... update instance
}

// ✅ EXTRACT TO METHOD
private void validateInstanceName(String name) {
    if (name == null || name.isBlank()) {
        throw new ValidationException("Name required");
    }
}

public Instance createInstance(CreateInstanceRequest req, User user) {
    validateInstanceName(req.getName());
    // ... create instance
}

public void updateInstance(UUID id, UpdateInstanceRequest req) {
    validateInstanceName(req.getName());
    // ... update instance
}
```

### ✅ DO: Use Immutability Where Possible

```java
// ✅ Use final for immutable fields
@Data
public class InstanceConfig {
    private final String engine;
    private final Integer memoryMb;
    private final String username;
    
    // No setters for final fields
}

// ✅ Collections should be unmodifiable
public List<Instance> getUserInstances(UUID userId) {
    return Collections.unmodifiableList(
        instanceRepository.findByUserId(userId)
    );
}
```

### ✅ DO: Validate at Boundaries

```java
// ✅ Validate in DTO with @Valid
@PostMapping
public ResponseEntity<InstanceResponse> createInstance(
    @Valid @RequestBody CreateInstanceRequest req
) {
    // Request is guaranteed valid here
    return ResponseEntity.ok(instanceService.create(req));
}

// ✅ Method assumes valid input
@Service
public class InstanceService {
    public Instance create(CreateInstanceRequest req) {
        // No validation needed - already validated by controller
        return instanceRepository.save(buildInstance(req));
    }
}
```

### ❌ DON'T: Hardcode Values

```java
// ❌ BAD: Hardcoded values
public Instance createInstance(CreateInstanceRequest req) {
    instance.setDefaultPort(3306);
    instance.setDefaultMemory(512);
}

// ✅ GOOD: Use constants or configuration
private static final int DEFAULT_MYSQL_PORT = 3306;
private static final int DEFAULT_INSTANCE_MEMORY_MB = 512;

@Value("${instance.default.memory:512}")
private int defaultMemory;

public Instance createInstance(CreateInstanceRequest req) {
    instance.setPort(DEFAULT_MYSQL_PORT);
    instance.setMemory(defaultMemory);
}
```

### ❌ DON'T: Mix Business Logic and Framework Code

```java
// ❌ BAD: Framework concerns in business logic
@Service
public class InstanceService {
    
    @Transactional
    @Cacheable("instances")
    public List<Instance> getInstances() {
        // Business logic mixed with Spring annotations
    }
}

// ✅ GOOD: Separate concerns
@Service
public class InstanceService {
    
    public List<Instance> getInstances() {
        // Pure business logic
        return instanceRepository.findAll();
    }
}

@Repository
public interface InstanceRepository extends JpaRepository<Instance, UUID> {
    
    @Cacheable("instances")
    @Query("SELECT i FROM Instance i WHERE i.deletedAt IS NULL")
    List<Instance> findAll();  // Framework concern here
}
```

---

## Code Review Checklist

- ✅ All public methods have Javadoc
- ✅ No obvious code duplication (DRY)
- ✅ Methods are focused (single responsibility)
- ✅ Meaningful variable and method names
- ✅ Constants used instead of magic values
- ✅ Proper exception handling (specific exceptions)
- ✅ No System.out or printStackTrace
- ✅ Use Optional instead of null checks
- ✅ Validation at boundaries (@Valid)
- ✅ Logging instead of printing
- ✅ No hardcoded configuration values
- ✅ Tests present for public methods
- ✅ No sensitive data in logs
- ✅ Lombok used appropriately
